summary: Bug 2 (Cavalry unable to declare) of issue #126: passing during Infantry Maneuvers (Phase.AttackDeclaration) with nothing to assign used to skip straight to Phase.Dynasty, bypassing Cavalry Maneuvers entirely -- a deliberate but incorrect design (the removed comment documented this as intended). Infantry and Cavalry Maneuvers are separate declaration steps; declining one must not skip the other. Fixed by routing an AttackDeclaration pass through the same DeclareAttack(Assignments:[]) path already used for a Cavalry Maneuvers pass, so it always proceeds to DefenseAssignment then CavalryDeclaration. This surfaced a second, previously-masked bug: UnresolvedBattlefields was set to every non-destroyed enemy province regardless of whether an attacker ever placed a unit there, which (once Cavalry Maneuvers could actually be reached with nothing attacking) produced a Battle Selection phase with zero legal choices -- a dead end. Fixed by computing UnresolvedBattlefields from the attacker's actual Zone.Battlefield presence, recomputed after both the Infantry and Cavalry declaration steps, and skipping straight to Dynasty when nothing is unresolved after Cavalry Defense.
validation: New PublishedTests.CavalryAfterEmptyInfantry: an Infantry-less attacker (only a Cavalry-keyword personality) passes Infantry Maneuvers, reaches CavalryDeclaration, and successfully assigns the Cavalry unit to a province. Updated Program.cs's Priority test, which had encoded the old bug (an all-empty attack still reaching BattleSelection with a selectable province) as expected behavior -- now asserts the correct outcome (Phase.Dynasty, zero UnresolvedBattlefields). Full suite: 85/85 + 34/34 + 8/8 tests pass. bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passes (5/5 server integration, 4/4 client transport).
remaining: Bug 3 from the same batch (attachments visually overlaying their Personality before settling into place) and the Doji Atsumichi bow/straighten once-per-turn quota fix are tracked separately.
